recheck.ruling: aurora-lint ADR-0011 6b28c8d7 (wpa_supplicant/Makefile:1004-1006, -rdynamic under CONFIG_DYNAMIC_EAP_METHODS), with hostapd/Makefile:112-116 (-rdynamic under CONFIG_WPA_TRACE) for files only hostapd links

notes:
A CORRECTION, NOT A NEW ADJUDICATION. hostap caller-set re-pass, the remaining directories, keys aurora-lint no longer reports.

RULING. aurora-lint ADR-0011 6b28c8d7: wpa_supplicant/Makefile:1004-1006 links with -ldl -rdynamic under CONFIG_DYNAMIC_EAP_METHODS, and hostapd/Makefile:112-116 links with -rdynamic under CONFIG_WPA_TRACE; both configurations compile (ADR-0010), so every non-static function in a file either binary links, and every static function whose address escapes (an ops table, a callback or eloop registration), has an open caller set, and in-tree call sites prove nothing. Also applied: an earlier dereference is not a check; documentation, an "internal invariant" and a third-party library contract are not proof; a closed static chain counts only while every call site provably passes a safe value; an in-function correlation counts when every writer is listed.

EXP34-C rows follow the site ruling (2026-09-21; EXP34-C/2026-10-07): the violation site is a dereference token on the keyed line itself; a line that only passes the pointer to an in-tree function is not a site (the callee's dereference is its own), and a dereference on another line of the same statement belongs to that line's key. Labels are keyed by line, so a line that is not a site for the pointer the old reason was about but dereferences a different pointer nothing proves non-null is TP on that dereference.

SCOPE. FP rows outside src/ap, hostapd/ and wpa_supplicant/ whose reason rested on callers, an earlier dereference, documentation or a mixed caller/local basis, in files linked into wpa_supplicant or hostapd, at keys aurora-lint d21be1b3d does not report (each row's provenance says so). Held out (9 rows): rows in files only a Windows (PE) build compiles, where the -rdynamic export premise is unsettled; one EXP34-C row whose only candidate site is a pointer passed to a third-party library function; API00-C rows that would turn on a parameter other than the one the old reason named; one API05-C row whose kept FP rested on precedent rather than a stated basis; and one row on the LOG_WOLF_ERROR_FUNC macro, whose call sites are all in-tree.

METHOD. Read-only research readers re-read every row at source at the pinned commit under a written brief that states the site ruling and the settled shapes up front, and drafted a verdict. Every EXP34-C draft was then re-checked at source against the site ruling on its keyed line. A fresh-context refuter re-read a sample of 30 rows (the rows the readers were least sure of, then a random draw): 26 upheld, 1 citation corrected, 3 overturned (FP -> TP: a pointer field read through a proven session pointer, written only from an escaping eloop context, was unproven); the same correction was applied to a fourth row of that shape outside the sample, and every kept EXP34-C FP was then scanned for a pointer field read through a proven pointer. Corrections were applied.

RESULT. 144 rows reviewed: FP->FP 73, FP->TP 71. Verdict changes by rule: EXP34-C 51, API00-C 20. 41 kept FP rows are "Not a dereference site". Every kept row's reason is restated to the basis it now rests on.

Mechanics: in-place edits keep each key; each original batch takes a row_count decrement and a superseded_rows record. Counting basis: distinct (project, commit, file, line, rule) keys. No precision claim is made here.
